title: DAPT for minor stroke and high-risk TIA
question: Who gets short-term DAPT after minor stroke or TIA, with which regimen, and for how long?
population: Noncardioembolic minor ischemic stroke or high-risk TIA
Did not receive IVT (all DAPT trials excluded IVT)

rules.condition: NIHSS ≤3 or ABCD2 ≥4, within 24 h of onset
rules.recommendation: Clopidogrel (with load) + aspirin, start within 24 h, 21 days, then SAPT
evidenceNote: Kleindorfer 2021: COR 1, LOE A — ideally within 12–24 h, at least within 7 days; 21–90 days

rules.condition: NIHSS ≤5 or ABCD2 ≥4 at 24–72 h, or NIHSS 4–5 within 24 h, with presumed atherosclerotic cause (≥50% stenosis likely causative, or new infarcts of presumed large-artery origin)
NIHSS ≤3 or ABCD2 ≥4, within 24 h, known CYP2C19 loss-of-function carrier
rules.recommendation: Ticagrelor + aspirin × 21 days, then ticagrelor alone, in preference to clopidogrel-based DAPT (CHANCE-2)

rules.condition: Noncardioembolic minor stroke (NIHSS ≤5) or high-risk TIA (ABCD2 ≥6, or symptomatic ≥50% intracranial/extracranial stenosis that could account for the TIA), <24 h, no IVT (THALES)
rules.recommendation: Ticagrelor + aspirin × 30 days may be considered (THALES) — more severe bleeding including ICH
evidenceNote: Kleindorfer 2021 §5.19: COR 2b, LOE B-R (SR) — used ≥30% stenosis for any event

rules.condition: Any regimen beyond 90 days, or adding a third antiplatelet
rules.recommendation: Don't — excess hemorrhage without added benefit
evidenceNote: Kleindorfer 2021: COR 3: Harm, LOE A (DAPT >90 days or triple therapy)
AHA 2026: triple antiplatelet COR 3: Harm, LOE B-R

rules.condition: Received IVT in the past 24 h
rules.recommendation: DAPT not studied after IVT; any antiplatelet in the first 24 h only with a compelling indication — usually after 24-h imaging
evidenceNote: AHA 2026: COR 2b, LOE B-NR (antiplatelets within 24 h of IVT)

rules.condition: Already on aspirin at the time of the event
rules.recommendation: Raising the dose or switching agents is of unclear benefit; DAPT criteria above still apply

options.doseText: Clopidogrel 300–600 mg load, then 75 mg daily; aspirin 160–325 mg load, then 75–100 mg daily
notes: CHANCE: 300 mg load, 21 days; POINT: 600 mg load, 90 days
Agent details, interactions and holds: see the agent entries

options.doseText: Ticagrelor 180 mg load, then 90 mg BID; aspirin 300–325 mg load (THALES) or 75–300 mg (CHANCE-2), then 75–100 mg daily
notes: Agent details, interactions and holds: see the agent entries

institutionVaries: CYP2C19 genotype testing availability and turnaround
pearls: Trial NNTs (AHA 2026 Table 9): CHANCE 28, INSPIRES 53, CHANCE-2 63, POINT 67, THALES 91; POINT, THALES, CHANCE-2 and INSPIRES had slightly more bleeding
In a large Italian registry only 7.8% of DAPT-treated patients met trial criteria (AHA 2026 knowledge gaps) — out-of-criteria use is untested

Stenosis thresholds differ by source: THALES enrollment and AHA 2026 use ≥50% as a high-risk-TIA criterion; Kleindorfer 2021 §5.19 used ≥30% for any event; ipsilateral >30% intracranial stenosis has its own recommendation (icad-symptomatic rule 3)
sources: Prabhakaran S, et al. 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2026;57:e316-e436. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000513
Kleindorfer DO, et al. 2021 Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2021;52:e364-e467. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000375
Johnston SC, et al. Ticagrelor and Aspirin or Aspirin Alone in Acute Ischemic Stroke or TIA (THALES). N Engl J Med 2020;383:207-217. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1916870
